acceptance.summary: CargoEvaluator now defaults to fail-closed untrusted execution in a disposable snapshot under Bubblewrap and a delegated cgroup v2. The host network and environment are removed, runtime mounts are read-only, the full snapshot root remains available for Cargo workspaces, aggregate memory/PID/CPU-time budgets apply to the entire descendant tree, timeouts kill the process group, and TrustedHost remains an explicit opt-in for trusted code and dependencies.
coverage: Bubblewrap user, mount, PID, IPC, UTS, cgroup and network namespaces with no host-network route
cleared environment, isolated HOME/CARGO_HOME/TMPDIR and offline Cargo
read-only runtime mounts with only the disposable snapshot writable
full snapshot-root bind with package_subdir used only as chdir for workspace and sibling path-dependency compatibility
delegated cgroup v2 memory.max, memory.swap.max, pids.max and cpu.max
aggregate max_cpu_seconds enforced from cpu.stat/usage_usec across multiple workers
pre-exec cgroup attachment, process-session kill, cgroup.kill teardown and bounded output drains
default/public/all-feature Clippy and tests, doctests, MSRV 1.89, Miri and Docker on exact candidate and integrated target
dynamic CI probe exercised secret isolation, absent network route, missing /etc/passwd and aggregate multi-process CPU exhaustion
limitations: This qualifies Linux Bubblewrap plus cgroup v2 containment, not a formal proof of the kernel, Bubblewrap or mounted toolchain.
Untrusted mode requires an explicitly delegated cgroup v2 root and pre-provisioned offline dependencies; missing capabilities fail closed.
No local Rust execution is claimed because Cargo was unavailable in the automation worker; local git diff --check passed and GitHub exact-head CI is authoritative.

GitHub branch-protection administration was inaccessible to the integration; the branch endpoint reported protected=false and repository rulesets were empty. No configured CI gate was weakened or bypassed.
